title: Transaction body write coalescing moonshot
impact: Moonshot: attacks the assumption that every awaited `tx.execute()` inside `db.transaction()` requires its own writer round-trip. Buffered concurrent (Future.wait-inside-tx) execute calls per Transaction and flushed them as a single `MultiExecuteRequest`; the writer's existing handler already tolerates `txDepth > 0` so each statement inherited the outer transaction and per-statement outcomes distributed back to individual futures. A fast path plus a `hasPendingWrites` guard on `drainForClose` held the common sequential-await pattern at pre-213 microtask cost. Focused `tx_body_write_coalescing.dart` measured **tx-burst-future-wait -26% / -31%** across order-flipped passes (ab_drift_check verdict: REPRODUCED); sequential-await, single-write, and interleaved-select lanes all below the 3% effect floor (verdict: neutral). Rejected: the pattern (`Future.wait([tx.execute × N])` specifically inside a transaction) is not one resqlite steers users toward — same-SQL bulk writes have `executeBatch`, different-SQL non-atomic bursts have exp 180's standalone coalescing, and different-SQL atomic bursts are rare. Accepting four load-bearing guards + persistent per-Transaction buffer state on the writer-path hot path for a workload we are not promoting was not worth the maintenance cost. Runtime prototype preserved at `archive/exp-213`; focused harness retained as durable gate for future transaction-body write experiments.
